title: Cosmic background production plan
status: 16 proposed backgrounds mapped to 24 playable chapters and one ending; no artwork generated by this plan.
style: Same hand-tinted astronomical chromolithograph, chalk and dry-gouache language as catalogue.json: midnight indigo, feathered ivory light, restrained warm amber, charcoal/copper rock and teal water. Broad continuous scenery, no circular frames or embedded labels.

framing.safe_setting_region: Recognizable setting high in the frame and along sides; allow lower and side crop in narrow/tall screens. Inspect full artwork on desktop too.
framing.requirement: The quiet region is a compositional target, not a runtime mask, wash or guaranteed exclusion zone. Review with actual 72px medallions and labels.

continuity.coast_camera: Face across the basin, stepped basalt headland LEFT, low inland ridge RIGHT, basin between. Same perspective and horizon in backgrounds 13, 14 and 16.
continuity.earth: One continuing cracked basalt and molten-orange Earth; no modern continents or living surface.
continuity.moon: Same pale early gray-ivory Moon after formation, no familiar dark maria.
continuity.discovery_timing: Background is static throughout its chapter; show entry conditions only. Derived outcomes belong to movable icons until a later chapter can safely adopt them.
continuity.backgrounds_are_not_inventory: No decorative isolated small objects, token borders, arrows, particle diagrams or apparent extra drag targets in scenery.

review_plan: Check every chapter entry against its listed do_not_show constraints and current manuscript, including optional recipe results.
Compare coast backgrounds 13, 14 and 16 together for matching headland silhouette, ridge direction, basin placement and horizon.
At 390px phone width check actual cropping and 72px icons with labels; pale rings, mineral textures and cloud edges must separate from the scene.
Inspect the quiet area at full desktop composition and shorter-phone crop; avoid bright lines behind names or false circular targets.
Check Earth and Moon chronology across space scenes and the ending; no early ocean, premature Moon, modern maria or biological scenery.

chapter_mapping.title: A gentler way to scatter a star
Fire on one side, frost on the other
Rock lets go of its water
The sea takes something from the stone

backgrounds.title: Before the first star
backgrounds.physical_depiction: Near-black indigo space with a broad barely luminous primordial gas veil feathering in from the upper left and right edges. A faint density knot lives high at the margin, leaving most of the scene dark and spacious. No bright point source.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: Primordial particles and gas are the initial physical setting; chapter 2 begins before its first star is made.
backgrounds.continuity: Use this same restrained gas language in primordial-gas, gathering-gas and the first-star family; no inherited solids in the first-star chapters.
backgrounds.composition: Portrait 390:844. Put broad recognizable setting in upper quarter and at edges. Preserve the central x=0.12–0.88, y=0.23–0.88 as low-contrast continuous scenery; no isolated medallion-like objects. Quietness is painted into the image. Keep essential geography away from extreme side and bottom crops.

backgrounds.title: At the edge of the massive star
backgrounds.physical_depiction: A huge cropped ivory-amber stellar limb curves across the very top and upper-right corner. Fine uneven luminous rays feather outward above the working area, while the lower three quarters fall into calm indigo. The surface is continuous and intact.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: A massive first star exists after chapter 2. The later interior burning sequence and supernova have not yet happened at their respective chapter entries.
backgrounds.continuity: Match first-star luminosity and ray language; show only a cropped portion so this reads as setting rather than an extra draggable star.

backgrounds.title: A different star grows old
backgrounds.physical_depiction: An expansive dark interstellar field with one broad gentle amber stellar glow entering from the upper-left edge. Its diffuse outer light gives the scene a slower, softer character than the massive star, with a deep quiet central field.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: The supplied lower-mass aging star belongs to a later generation. Giant expansion, carbon shedding and exposed core are outcomes to be made.
do_not_show: supernova remnants copied from the prior star
backgrounds.continuity: Introduce the later-giant warm light family without painting its evolved outcome or implying it is the preceding neutron-star remnant.

backgrounds.title: The interstellar reservoir
backgrounds.physical_depiction: Broad quiet blue-indigo gas fields with soft charcoal occlusion at the upper margins and feathered ivory light outside the cloud. Sparse grain-like print texture belongs to the medium, not individually illustrated physical dust. A dark central cavity is visual breathing room, not a scientific tunnel.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: The setting is a mixed interstellar reservoir after stellar generations. Chapter 6 makes condensed solids; chapter 7 makes ice on grain surfaces.
backgrounds.continuity: Shared cloud atmosphere for enrichment and shielded grain chemistry. No picture claims that invisible chemical abundance is visibly colour-coded.

backgrounds.title: The cloud before the Sun
backgrounds.physical_depiction: A long dark feathered molecular-cloud filament enters from the top and curls gently toward an off-centre upper knot. The knot remains unlit. Dusty edges taper into a broad calm blue-black centre and lower field.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: Cold molecular material and a contracting filament precede the chapter; the Sun and disk are this chapter’s discoveries.
backgrounds.continuity: Match cloud-filament shape. The later solar disk will inherit the same approximate upper-right centre when it appears in the next background.

backgrounds.physical_depiction: The already formed solar disk is a very broad cropped diagonal arc across the upper edge, warm near a small partly cropped ivory Sun at upper right and cooler farther left. Its lower edge fades into indigo before the play area. Individual solids are unresolved.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: The young Sun and its disk are goals completed in chapter 8. Heat processing and planetesimal growth remain to be performed.
backgrounds.continuity: Use the solar-disk tilt, source position and warm-to-cool gradient from the item family. Quiet centre is dark disk atmosphere, not a blank overlay.

backgrounds.title: Among the small worlds
backgrounds.physical_depiction: An irregular rocky planetesimal surface is cropped into the upper-left edge and a dim ice-patched small body is partly visible at the far upper right. They are widely separated by dark space. Both surfaces are cool and unbroken; interior structure is hidden.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: Rocky and icy planetesimals exist after chapter 10. Internal melting, layered interiors and water-rock alteration are the discoveries in chapter 11.
backgrounds.continuity: Use the same irregular small-body silhouettes as the inventory family; keep bodies large and cropped rather than scattered like extra inventory.

backgrounds.title: Gas still surrounds the outer disk
backgrounds.physical_depiction: A broad faint outer solar-disk arc crosses the upper frame with a distant warm point of solar light far to one side. Cool gas wisps remain continuous but diffuse; a few unresolved pale solid streaks lie in the uppermost margin. Most of the field is deep blue-black.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: Outer-disk material and small icy bodies already exist; core growth and gas envelopes are this chapter’s outcomes.
backgrounds.continuity: Same solar system as background-06 but a more distant view. Avoid inventing a new star or a sharply bounded snow line.

backgrounds.title: Crowded paths in the inner system
backgrounds.physical_depiction: Dim overlapping arcs of the inner dusty disk surround a distant cropped Sun. One broad rough small-body limb enters the upper-left edge; a second far smaller fragment is deeply embedded in the upper dust context. Leave the centre quiet without drawn orbital diagrams.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: Small rocky bodies and fragment reservoirs precede planetary embryos. Earth and Theia have not been selected or assembled yet.
backgrounds.continuity: Return to the warmer inner-disk illumination established in background-06. Cropped rough limb belongs to the planetesimal family.

backgrounds.title: The growing Earth
backgrounds.physical_depiction: The upper edge holds a large cropped curved limb of the established young Earth: charcoal rocky skin crossed by sparse narrow amber seams, with black space below and around it. The surface is hot but no full magma ocean or interior cutaway is exposed. A dim warm haze stays close to the limb.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: Young Earth exists at chapter 14 entry. Its interior is differentiated by chapter 15, but the collision has not happened.
do_not_show: a whole global magma ocean before chapter 14 creates it
backgrounds.continuity: One Earth with the catalogue’s charcoal-and-orange material language; retain the broad limb curvature in post-impact backgrounds. At chapter 15 this is a compatible external view of an already differentiated interior.

backgrounds.title: After the giant impact
backgrounds.physical_depiction: A large cropped remelted Earth limb at the top glows orange between dark disrupted basalt patches. A diffuse broken arc of hot rocky debris passes behind and above it, thinning toward the upper side corners. The central and lower field remains open dark space.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: The surviving impact Earth and bound Moon-forming disk are both completed goals in chapter 15.
do_not_show: a solid ring glued to an orbit
backgrounds.continuity: Carry Earth’s limb and disk tilt from the impact-system and lunar-disk icons. There is one surviving Earth, never a replacement planet.

backgrounds.title: The hot planet releases its inventory
backgrounds.physical_depiction: A close cropped Earth limb across the upper frame has orange silicate exposed between dark irregular surviving patches. The broad lower field is dark space with faint amber spill close to the limb; there is no opaque atmosphere, new crustal coast or discrete gas plume yet.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: Post-impact Earth has been reworked and the Moon has cooled in chapter 16. Outgassing, a steam-rich sky and the fresh volcanic surface are this chapter’s outcomes.
backgrounds.continuity: Same Earth as backgrounds 10 and 11, moving closer to its surface. The next scene will descend to the local coast after that landscape is made.

backgrounds.title: Bare rock below a heavy sky
backgrounds.physical_depiction: A low bare volcanic landscape establishes the recurring geography: blunt stepped basalt headland at upper left, low inland ridge at upper right, shallow dry basin between. A small distant lava seam glows near the far left margin. Heavy dim gray-indigo atmospheric haze lies above. The foreground is broad low-contrast basalt and the central basin stays empty.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: Chapter 17 has made solid rock, active lava and a steam-rich atmosphere. Chapter 18 must make surviving liquid rain; chapter 19 must accumulate the sea.
backgrounds.continuity: This is the coast master camera. Lock the stepped headland on the left, right inland ridge, basin outline and foreground rock angles for all later coast scenes. Keep the lava distant so local cooling states remain legible in icons.

backgrounds.title: The young sea and the bare coast
backgrounds.physical_depiction: Using exactly the coast master camera, a broad subdued teal sea now fills the basin between the stepped left basalt headland and the low right inland ridge. A rough unsorted dark rocky edge occupies only the margins; the centre is calm low-detail water. Dim ivory ambient light grazes the upper horizon. No bright Moon or reflection path appears.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: The sea is completed in chapter 19. Chemical weathering, beaches, tides and the final reflected-light outcomes must remain discoveries of their own chapters. Reusing a rocky stretch avoids asserting optional later states.
do_not_show: rounded pebble shore before it is made
backgrounds.continuity: Exact headland, ridge and basin silhouette inherited from background-13; water occupies the previously empty low ground. Show a persistent rocky margin rather than repainting it into a chapter outcome. Use the same baseline for chapter 24 so its moonlight remains a visible discovery.

backgrounds.title: Beneath the sea
backgrounds.physical_depiction: A quiet deep teal underwater field with the rough dark seafloor rising gently at the bottom side edges. Two modest connected rock fissures lie near the upper side of the floor, leaving the centre open and dim. No bright vent or plume is present. The water surface is out of view.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: The sea and bare underwater crust exist before hydrothermal circulation. Open fractures are supplied at chapter entry.
do_not_show: bubbles implying all hot water boils
backgrounds.continuity: Same basalt fracture language as the coast, seen underwater. Match the hydrothermal-loop cross-section’s left descent and right return geometry without painting the arrows or flow before creation.

backgrounds.title: A sea beneath the Moon
backgrounds.physical_depiction: Return to the exact coast master camera under deep indigo night. The early pale gray-ivory Moon hangs high above the bare basin, without dark maria. A modest broken ivory reflection crosses the broad teal sea. The left basalt headland and right low ridge remain recognizable silhouettes, and the foreground remains dark quiet rock. No separate detailed pool reflection is required.
backgrounds.entry_state_basis: The sea, pale early Moon and at least one moonlight ending are complete before this chapter. This is the first background permitted to celebrate the finished moonlit scene.
do_not_show: a required second ending outcome such as a specific mirrored pool
backgrounds.continuity: Same landforms and camera as backgrounds 13 and 14. Moon uses the pale-moon anchor; final broad-sea light is soft enough to suit either selected ending. Could also supply cover art if requested by the parent task.
